report.summary: The new cache tasks, change classifier, fixture outputs and per-test cleanup in workspace-rpc look right. One blocking problem: ops.test.ts makes 'step runner rules' a parallel group, but one of its tests changes the shared STEP_LIMITS['settings.read'] to 300 ms while other tests in the group run settings.read. That can make them fail at random, and it breaks the rule this branch adds: groups that change global state run one test at a time.

findings.text: 'step runner rules' is now describe.concurrent, but the test 'aborts a step at its timeout…' (lines 1937-1950) changes the shared STEP_LIMITS['settings.read'] to timeoutMs: 300 and only restores it in finally. The other tests in the group ('recovery after a DO restart…' x2, 'a step's timing includes…') run create ops that call settings.read at the same time, so they can pick up the 300 ms timeout under load: settings.read is aborted, retried and skipped, and those tests fail at random. This breaks the new AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md rule that groups changing global state run one test at a time. Move this test into a group that runs in order (e.g. 'create op'), or keep 'step runner rules' in order.

The phone-chromium project now only runs tests tagged @mobile, so the phone-only branches in the git primary action test (and the phone test.skip lines around 291/311) never run on a phone. Remove the dead branches or tag the test so the code doesn't look like phone coverage it no longer has.

The documentation-only path runs only oxlint and oxfmt, and both are set to ignore docs/**, so a docs/-only change gets almost no real checking. Allowed, since the required check still passes, but CI.md should say so plainly.
